title: NUERS document-alignment audit
verdict: Partially aligned. Not ready for production acceptance or a claim of complete BIR/ESP compliance.
scope: Localhost source, migrations, read-only aggregate runtime checks, existing tests and isolated dummy-data diagnostic probes. No application fixes or real-record modifications were made in this audit. Live Plesk and infrastructure were not audited.
source_precedence: User-supplied RMC and Annex A are the regulatory baseline for this comparison; the blank checklist is not accreditation evidence.
ESP deck is supporting guidance. Annex A has 17 items; slides 32-33 omit joint-venture item 8 and renumber subsequent items.
NUERS v1.1/v2 specifications define project acceptance/design requirements and explicitly are not BIR approval.
Focused official-domain web searches returned no matching publication; this audit does not independently authenticate the supplied circular or certify legal compliance.

production_blockers: Verified BIR-issued solution accreditation certificate is not recorded.
A current accreditation validity period is required.
Annex A documentary requirements are incomplete or unverified.
All seven mandatory BIR accreditation stages must pass.
Taxpayer PTI Electronic Invoice authority and supporting evidence are required; CAS PTU/AC is insufficient.
Written client-taxpayer authorization is required for ESP integration services.
Current taxpayer EIS certification is required.
Taxpayer Permit to Transmit is required separately from PTI.
BIR production credentials and key material are not registered.
Verified BIR production transport is not implemented; certification acknowledgements are simulations.

diagnostic_probes.database: isolated SQLite :memory: with dummy records only
diagnostic_probes.note: Probe success means the reported gaps reproduced; it is not compliance success.

findings.title: Anonymous client-account writes and deletion cascade
requirements: RMC pp.2,8-11: integrity, authorized access, preservation and confidentiality
Functional v1.1 pp.2-3,18; v2 pp.2-3,12-15: role/tenant scope and controlled changes
findings.verified: Isolated anonymous PATCH changed dummy account status and balance. Anonymous DELETE removed the dummy client account and its linked users/profiles rows. Both returned HTTP 200.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated callers can modify account state and erase linked login identity if this route is reachable. No real records were used in these tests.
findings.remediation: Retire generic account writes or require authenticated, explicit role/tenant authorization and allowed fields on every operation. Preserve identities and evidence via an approved deactivation workflow; prevent deletion without controlled policy.
findings.acceptance: Anonymous/wrong-role/cross-tenant PATCH and DELETE fail before any side effect. Admin deletion and account deactivation follow reviewed preservation policy.

findings.title: Anonymous generic identity and financial reads
requirements: RMC pp.2,6,9-10: security, confidentiality and authorized data access
Functional v1.1 p.2; v2 pp.2-3 and per-screen access requirements
findings.verified: Isolated unauthenticated GETs for profiles and merchant_transactions returned HTTP 200 and dummy rows. Merchant special checks and profile write checks do not protect the other generic GET operations.
findings.impact: Financial and identity records can be exposed without authentication; optional request filters are not tenant authorization.
findings.remediation: Apply centralized authentication, default-deny role policies, server-derived tenant/branch filters and response-field allowlists to all generic reads; preferably replace these routes with explicit scoped controllers.
findings.acceptance: Anonymous reads return 401, disallowed roles return 403, and another tenant cannot read records by omitting/changing filters.

findings.title: Legacy merchant invoice calculation trusts client-supplied totals
requirements: RMC pp.4,8,11: accurate, complete invoice and sales data
Functional v2 pp.6,16; v1.1 p.18: authoritative validation before issuance
findings.verified: Pure-method probe supplied quantity 2 x unit price 10000 centavos, but line_total/total_amount 1 centavo. The calculator accepted PHP 0.01 instead of recomputing PHP 200. No invoice was created.
findings.impact: Once issuance permissions are granted, the legacy path can persist inconsistent amounts. The newer draft-center calculator does not protect this endpoint.
findings.remediation: Use one server-side integer-money calculation service with approved tax/discount classifications, explicit rounding, and reconciliation/rejection of supplied totals.
findings.acceptance: Tampered lines, totals, VAT and discounts cannot change authoritative computed amounts; preview, stored document, API and exports agree.

findings.title: Sales summary counts duplicate references and omits standalone issued invoices
requirements: RMC pp.8-9: non-duplication and automatic SLS
Functional v2 p.10: exclude double counting and apply approved credit/debit/void treatment
findings.verified: An isolated fixture with two successful transaction rows carrying the same invoice identity returned sales PHP 224 while both were flagged duplicate. A separate issued business_invoices row was absent because the report is based on merchant_transactions.
findings.impact: The current operational sales report cannot establish complete/nonduplicated SLS compliance across all issuance paths.
findings.remediation: Define the canonical issued-document reporting ledger, stable document identity, conflict-review handling, complete source coverage and approved adjustment rules; validate the prescribed BIR output format.
findings.acceptance: Known duplicates/conflicts do not silently inflate approved totals; every in-scope issued document is reported exactly once, with traceable credit/debit/void rules and reconciliation to source.

findings.title: Verified BIR adapter, signing and authoritative response processing are absent
requirements: RMC pp.3-9: approved end-to-end issuance/transmission and testing
Functional v2 pp.2,8,16-17; v1.1 p.18: authenticated official responses and uncertainty handling
findings.verified: transport_implemented is false and production transmission is blocked. The browser helper called signInvoice produces a SHA-256 digest/checksum, not a private-key digital signature. Integration configuration/local diagnostics do not implement official token exchange or BIR response authentication.
findings.impact: No verified live BIR submission, acceptance, signing/encryption protocol, token refresh or timeout-result inquiry can be claimed.
findings.remediation: Obtain verified official interface/schema material and authorized certification credentials; implement a reviewed adapter, true signing/key management, authenticated response mapping and unknown-result inquiry. Keep production blocked until acceptance evidence exists.
findings.acceptance: BIR-authorized certification tests demonstrate schema, authentication, signing/encryption, acknowledgment, rejection, replay and ambiguous timeout behavior.

findings.title: Issued-document to durable outbox and delivery worker are incomplete
requirements: RMC pp.4,8-9: timely queuing, retries, reconciliation and recovery
Functional v2 pp.2,8,16; v1.1 p.18: atomic issuance/outbox and durable jobs
findings.verified: Invoice issuance and administrative EIS queuing are separate workflows. Retry rows and bounded backoff exist, but no production delivery Job/consumer or scheduled outbox dispatcher was found; runtime queue connection is sync.
findings.impact: Recorded deadlines do not guarantee automatic delivery/recovery or deadline escalation; cross-boundary crashes and uncertain acknowledgments have no completed acceptance flow.
findings.remediation: Persist canonical issuance, audit event and uniquely keyed outbox atomically; add leased durable workers, attempt evidence, inquiry-before-replay, escalation and crash recovery tests.
findings.acceptance: Crash/replay tests at each commit boundary demonstrate no lost/double documents; verified restoration preserves original deadline and completes authorized recovery.

findings.title: Privileged MFA, granular duties and independent approvals are incomplete
requirements: Functional v1.1 pp.2-3,18 and v2 pp.2-3,13,15-16
RMC p.6 and Annex A 14-15: demonstrable identity/access/security controls
findings.verified: Password/Google identity and same-device token behavior exist. No complete enforced MFA challenge/enrollment/recovery implementation was found. Password login has no dedicated throttle declaration; generic API defaults are not an account-aware login lockout policy. Broad staff roles do not implement the complete operator/auditor/security/branch duty matrix or two-person sensitive approvals.
findings.impact: Device binding and role checks do not satisfy the specified stronger privileged authentication and separation of duties.
findings.remediation: Add server-enforced privileged MFA, account/IP throttling, explicit action/tenant/branch policies, independent approver records and an approved bearer/cookie/token lifecycle.
findings.acceptance: Privileged actions fail without the required second factor and approval; cross-role/branch cases fail; stale/revoked credentials cannot retain access.

findings.title: Merchant profile edits bypass reviewed taxpayer identity changes
requirements: RMC pp.4,8: taxpayer identity, authority and traceability
Functional v2 pp.11-12: reviewed identity and readiness
findings.verified: The owner-scoped account endpoint can directly update merchant TIN, business name, tax/RDO/address fields. It does not invoke the registry revision/review or a complete authority revalidation workflow.
findings.impact: A reviewed taxpayer record can change through a separate route while existing approval references remain associated with its merchant ID.
findings.remediation: Route material identity edits through pending-change review, canonical duplicate-TIN validation, revisions, before/after audit evidence and re-evaluation of linked authorities.
findings.acceptance: Material taxpayer identity changes cannot preserve prior production eligibility without the required review; historical financial snapshots remain unchanged.

findings.title: Security, continuity and report screens contain unmeasured assurances
requirements: RMC pp.7-9 and Annex A 15-16: demonstrated operational/security/continuity evidence
Functional v2 pp.4,13-16: authoritative telemetry and real workflows
findings.verified: BCDR declares fixed successful backups, recovery results/sites and readiness. SOC/system charts use Math.random. Generic report generation reports success via timers/toasts. Main dashboard health is read from stored health rows, not an active measurement/freshness acceptance check.
findings.impact: These rendered screens do not establish current backup, DR, security, SLA or compliance performance. The newer real monitor does not make the legacy screens authoritative.
findings.remediation: Clearly label prototypes/unverified values or replace them with persisted measured telemetry, real report jobs, freshness rules and actual restore/failover evidence.
findings.acceptance: Every operational assurance links to a current measured job/result/evidence record; failed or absent evidence cannot display verified success.

findings.title: Protected evidence custody, legal holds and exit/delivery workflows are incomplete
requirements: RMC pp.9-10 and Annex A 14-17: continued access, complete secure extracts, legal holds and migration conditions
Functional v2 pp.12-16
findings.verified: Evidence references, CSV/JSON exports and a hash-chained application journal exist. No complete protected evidence-file repository, enforceable hold lifecycle, approved migration release/deletion flow or regulator request/delivery deadline workflow was demonstrated. Archive examples and local backups are not proof of these controls.
findings.impact: Reference fields and export buttons alone do not establish protected evidence custody or the complete preservation/access obligations.
findings.remediation: Implement protected evidence objects/manifests, independent audit checkpoints, enforceable holds, scoped secure export/delivery jobs, request deadlines and controlled migration/retention release conditions.
findings.acceptance: Holds prevent all relevant deletion paths; complete exports remain available through unpaid fees/exit; authorized delivery and migration confirmation are auditable.

findings.title: Capacity, residency, independent security assurance and full UTC normalization remain unproven
requirements: RMC pp.6-9; Annex A 14-17
Functional v2 pp.2,16: UTC persistence, realistic load and failure acceptance
findings.verified: Runtime persists many records under Asia/Manila while the audit journal explicitly uses UTC. Operational reports load collections and aggregate them in application memory. Functional tests do not establish independent assessments, data residency, measured load, restore/failover or the historical three-year capacity threshold.
findings.impact: No enterprise performance or infrastructure compliance acceptance can be concluded from table counts, screenshots or 89 functional tests.
findings.remediation: Define one time-persistence contract and conversion plan; test realistic data/query/export volumes; obtain independently verifiable security, residency, three-year track record and BIR-supervised continuity/performance evidence.
findings.acceptance: Approved load/recovery targets are measured end to end, residency/access arrangements are evidenced, and UTC/PHT boundary tests cover all transactional paths.

priority_order: Close anonymous generic account/identity/financial endpoints and their mutation/cascade paths.
Unify financial calculation and canonical complete/nonduplicated SLS reporting.
Enforce taxpayer identity change review, granular authorization, privileged MFA and independent approvals.
Complete atomic issuance/outbox, durable workers, official BIR adapter, authentic responses and uncertain-result reconciliation.
Replace prototype operational assurances with measured evidence; complete evidence custody, holds, portability and manual contingency workflows.
Complete independent security/residency/capacity and BIR-supervised performance/continuity acceptance before production.
limitations: A passing functional test suite does not certify accreditation, security or high-volume resilience.
Aggregate approval counts reflect records available in the audited localhost database at the recorded runtime time.
Official BIR technical schemas and production certification access were not available for protocol acceptance.
No compliance percentage is assigned because software controls, legal authority and independently verified evidence have different acceptance conditions.
